newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says to decree most pending labor laws.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says to decree most pending labor laws.

text.p: All but one of Argentina's pending labor reforms will be introduced by presidential decree, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Thursday.
He told reporters the only exception would be a new and less costly severance payment system which requires congressional approval.
Fernandez said the government was issuing decrees because the country's powerful trade unions had blocked reforms in Congress and this could endanger World Bank credits.
President Carlos Menem Wednesday signed three decrees cutting the wage bargaining power of the unions and eroding their monopoly on health insurance schemes.
Fernandez, who leaves Friday for talks with bankers in New York, said ongoing negotiations with the unions had served only to postpone the start of the new health fund system.
Menem's decrees, which sparked general strike threats, were signed after talks with labour chiefs ended in a stalement and reform bills stalled in Congress.
